title: Agur and Lemuel
lead: Agur son of Jakeh and King Lemuel, whose mother taught him, are the two named authors of Proverbs 30 and 31:1–9. Neither appears anywhere else in the Bible, and both may have been wise men from outside Israel, perhaps from the Arabian people of Massa.

sections.h: Two sages at the end of Proverbs
sections.b:
Proverbs names its authors in headings: Solomon (1:1; 10:1; 25:1), "the wise" (22:17; 24:23), Agur (30:1) and Lemuel (31:1). Agur confesses that he has no wisdom of his own, asks who has gone up to heaven, and trusts God's tested word (30:2–6). His prayer for neither poverty nor riches (30:7–9) is the only prayer in the book. Lemuel's words are really his mother's: a queen mother's warning against women and wine and her charge to speak for the poor (31:2–9).

Both headings contain the word massa', "oracle", which is also the name of a son of Ishmael (Genesis 25:14). If it is the tribe, both men were Arabian sages, like Job's friends from the East, and their words show Israel gathering wisdom from its neighbors (1 Kings 4:30). Jewish tradition made both names titles of Solomon (Kohelet Rabbah 1:1), and the Talmud makes Lemuel's mother Bathsheba (Bavli Sanhedrin 70b).
